name: handler_tutorial
title: A progressr handler useful for Futureverse tutorials

origin.description: Choose the progress package or the cli package and keep the bar when the work finishes.
origin.usage: handler_tutorial(..., spec = c("progress", "cli"), type = "time", clear = FALSE)

arguments.name: spec
arguments.text: "progress" or "cli". match.arg accepts a unique prefix. The default is progress.

arguments.name: type
arguments.text: The format preset passed to the selected handler. The default is "time".

arguments.name: clear
arguments.text: When FALSE, the finished bar is left on the terminal. The default is FALSE.
Further arguments passed to the selected handler.

origin.details: spec cli returns handler_cli. spec progress returns handler_progress. A missing package stops with the install message.
origin.value: A progression handler. spec cli has first class cli_progression_handler.
origin.example:
h <- handler_tutorial(spec = "cli", enable = TRUE)
cat(sprintf("handler_tutorial spec cli is %s, clear %s, target %s.\n", class(h)[1], environment(h)$clear, environment(h)$target))

translation.description: Choose the cli handler and keep the bar when the work finishes. spec progress calls handler_progress.

arguments.name: spec
arguments.text: "progress" or "cli". A unique prefix matches. The default is progress.

arguments.name: type
arguments.text: The format preset passed to the selected handler. The default is "time".

arguments.name: clear
arguments.text: When False, the finished bar is left on the terminal. The default is False.

arguments.name: args
arguments.text: Further arguments passed to the selected handler.

translation.details: spec cli returns handler_cli with clear False and target terminal. spec progress calls handler_progress, which this translation does not define. The install error is raised only when the selected package is missing.
translation.value: A calling handler. spec cli has first class cli_progression_handler.
translation.example:
from progressr.cli_handlers import handler_tutorial

handler = handler_tutorial(spec="cli", enable=True)
clear = "TRUE" if handler._env["clear"] else "FALSE"
print(f"handler_tutorial spec cli is {handler.classes[0]}, clear {clear}, target {handler._env['target']}.")
